original_question: If two division algebras have the same splitting fields inside a specified class of field extensions, for example finite extensions or extensions of transcendence degree at most one, must they generate the same subgroup of the Brauer group?
target_in_paper: Section 10, Problem 10.3: determine whether two division algebras that have the same splitting fields in a given class (for example, finite extensions or extensions of transcendence degree at most one) must generate the same subgroup in the Brauer group. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual formulation. It correctly focuses on two division algebras, compares their splitting fields only within a chosen class of field extensions, gives the same sample classes used in the paper (finite extensions and extensions of transcendence degree at most one), and asks for equality of the subgroup generated in the Brauer group rather than for isomorphism of the algebras. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
missing_details: The two algebras should be understood as being over a common base field F. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
In the paper’s ambient terminology, an “F-division algebra” means a central simple F-algebra that is a division algebra. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
The class should be described as a class C of field extensions E/F, and the hypothesis is quantified over all E in C. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))

“Having the same splitting fields in C” should be made explicit as: for every E/F in C, E splits D if and only if E splits D'. The background defines splitting as D ⊗_F E being split. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
The ambient group should be named as Br(F), not just “the Brauer group.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
The conclusion is about the cyclic subgroups generated by the Brauer classes [D] and [D'] in Br(F). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
Problem 10.3 is stated without any degree, period, or characteristic restriction; your draft leaves that implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))

The nearby motivation is that this is a finer question than asking about all splitting fields: Theorem 10.1 gives strong information in the unrestricted setting. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
refined_question: Let F be a field, let D and D' be F-division algebras, and let C be a specified class of field extensions E/F (for example, all finite extensions, or all extensions of transcendence degree at most 1 over F). Suppose that for every E/F in C, E splits D if and only if E splits D'. Must the Brauer classes [D] and [D'] generate the same cyclic subgroup of Br(F)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
justification: The closest paper-faithful target is Problem 10.3 in Section 10. Section 10 first recalls Amitsur’s results: Theorem 10.1 says that having all splitting fields almost determines the algebra, and that isomorphic generic splitting fields force the same Brauer subgroup. The paper then explicitly asks the finer question in Problem 10.3 using exactly the examples that appear in your draft. Section 0 supplies the needed background on F-division algebras, splitting fields, and the Brauer group. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
